questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to make sweets and cakes at home for less money
The sugar in our food and how much is too much
Why fat is much worse for our health than sugar
How sugar is produced from sugar cane and beet
questions.why: Neil says they are talking about sugar and asks 'how much is too much?'

questions.q: Where does Rob say some sugar is hidden?
options: Only in sweets, cakes and fizzy drinks for children
Mainly in fresh fruit such as bananas and grapes
In meat and fish that has been kept in the freezer
In 'healthy' foods like yoghurts and fruit drinks
questions.why: He says some sugar is hidden in 'healthy' foods such as yoghurts, low fat snacks and fruit drinks.

questions.q: What does Rob say about the information on food packets?
options: He reads it, but finds it confusing
He never reads it
He finds it very clear and useful
He thinks it is always wrong
questions.why: Rob checks it, but says it can be very confusing because there's so much information.

questions.q: What does green mean in the colour coding on some packaging?
options: High levels of sugar, salt or fat
Medium levels
Low levels
The food is organic
questions.why: Neil says red is high, orange is medium and green is low.

questions.q: How much sugar did the man in Chester think was in the fat-free yoghurt?
options: None at all
About half the pot
About a third of the pot
A couple of teaspoons
questions.why: He said he'd 'probably think maybe a couple of teaspoonfuls'.

questions.q: How much of the yoghurt was actually sugar?
options: About a third
About a tenth
About half
About 5%
questions.why: The reporter says about a third of the yoghurt pot is actually sugar.

questions.q: Why does the man mention that the yoghurt says 'fat-free'?
options: He wants to buy more of it
He thinks fat-free food tastes worse
The label made him think it was healthy
He is on a diet with no fat
questions.why: He is amazed a third is sugar 'and it does say it's fat-free', so he expected it to be healthy.

questions.q: What is Dr Gunter Kuhnle's view?
options: Sugar should be avoided at all costs, especially by children
Don't make one nutrient seem evil; eat a balanced diet and enjoy food
Fat is the real problem, not sugar, so we should eat less of it
People should stop eating any kind of processed food completely
questions.why: He says demonising one food is 'the wrong way forward' and we should eat a balanced diet and enjoy it.
